brief.situation: 02:40 on a progressive care unit. Mrs. Duarte, 76, is day two after a large anterior myocardial infarction treated with a stent. She is restless and says she can't get comfortable lying down.
handover: Echo yesterday: ejection fraction 30%. Blood pressure 104/66 at midnight, heart rate 98, urine about 40 mL an hour until then.
Orders: oxygen to keep SpO2 at or above 90%, strict intake and output, and the rapid response team called for a systolic under 90, new confusion or urine under 30 mL an hour.
The night provider and the rapid response team are reachable at once.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Assess and act as you think the patient needs. Each assessment takes the time on its button.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Mrs. Duarte is confused, cold and barely making urine. What is happening, and what do you do?

parts.label: What is happening
parts.criteria: Systolic under 90, cold clammy skin, confusion and urine under 30 mL an hour after a large MI with an EF of 30%, with crackles and raised neck veins, are cardiogenic shock (cold and wet).
parts.modelAnswer: This is cardiogenic shock: low pressure, cold and clammy, confused, hardly any urine, after a big MI with an EF of 30%. She's also wet: crackles and raised neck veins.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Rapid response and cardiology now for vasoactive support and the cardiac ICU; keep her up on oxygen; no large fluid bolus; hand off.
parts.modelAnswer: Rapid response and cardiology now for support and the cardiac ICU, keep her sitting up on oxygen, no fluid bolus into wet lungs, and hand off.

unsafe.headline: Fluid into a wet heart
unsafe.body: Cold and wet means the pump has failed, not the tank. A large bolus can cause flash pulmonary edema.

worsened.headline: Arrest
worsened.body: Falling pressure with poor perfusion after a large MI is cardiogenic shock; call at the first criterion.

wrongRoute.headline: Left until morning
wrongRoute.body: New confusion with hypotension and oliguria is shock, not night-time delirium.

target.headline: Escalated in time
target.body: You sat her up, checked perfusion and urine, and called the shock within minutes. That is the expert path.

recovered.headline: ICU, with delays
recovered.body: Check how long the shock criteria went before the call.

time_up.headline: Still in shock
time_up.body: Cardiogenic shock is escalated within minutes.

scoring.modelReasoning: A large anterior MI with an EF of 30% is at risk of cardiogenic shock. She sits up on oxygen, her urine is measured hourly, and her perfusion checked. A systolic under 90 with cold, clammy skin, confusion and urine under 30 mL an hour, with crackles and raised neck veins, is cardiogenic shock, cold and wet: rapid response and cardiology now. A large fluid bolus would flood her lungs.

sigQ.ask: While you assess: which set of findings fits cardiogenic shock?

choices.label: Low pressure, cold clammy skin, confusion, low urine
Low pressure with warm, flushed skin

sigQ.explain: Clinical signs: altered mental status, cold or clammy skin or extremities, decreased urine output; objectively a lactate over 2 and urine under 30 mL an hour.
